records.mutation: replace the abstract intersect-across-readings clause with an audit-before-discarding rule plus a both-members/symmetric-case test and a second-independent-route verification
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent scored 0/8; two rollouts hit the 16384 cap and all eight burned 13.4k-16.4k tokens, one repeating 'impossible' 130 times. The decisive evidence: six rollouts explicitly constructed the balanced pair where the two picks coincide, verified it against the stated conditions, then talked themselves out of it on a self-invented knowledge claim and reported a factor of the shown number instead. So the binding failure is no longer a missing concept or bad ordering but discarding a candidate that already passed. The incumbent's intersect-across-live-readings clause is too abstract to fire before the budget is gone, so I replaced it with an audit-the-discard rule, an explicit demand to impose each constraint on both members of the pair (which surfaces the symmetric case), and a concrete second-route verification as the stopping condition.

records.mutation: replace the generic clashing-check clause with (a) an irreversible-step guard (divisor zeros, extraneous roots after squaring/clearing) and (b) a widen-the-assumed-form rule for when a supposedly constant quantity comes out varying
records.subagent_summary: Only 6 of 8 fresh rollouts scored; both failures hit the 16384-token cap with no stated value. Both derived the correct reduction and then computed the modulus of each root, found it varying, and concluded the setup or the problem must be broken - they spent thousands of tokens relitigating sound algebra. One eventually recovered the general conic form and verified it, but too late to report. The real defect is a too-narrow assumption (an origin-centered locus, i.e. constant modulus) being read as a contradiction. So I replaced the incumbent's vague recheck-that-line advice with a concrete widen-the-assumed-form rule, plus a transferable guard on the irreversible steps (vanishing divisors, extraneous roots from squaring or clearing denominators) that generate such conflicts elsewhere.

records.mutation: generalize the containment trap to a bigger-never-swallows rule with a no-uncomputed-ratios ban, and swap the qualitative trade test for exact simplest-case computation plus a bound-and-witness stop licence
records.subagent_summary: Six of eight scored, so the sum-minus-overlap frame is kept. Both failures were geometric, not budget: one concluded that because every side of the large piece sits distance 1 from its center while the small piece reaches only 0.5, the small piece is swallowed at every angle, so it reported the plain larger area and stopped early with tokens to spare; the other never closed reasoning, oscillating between whole-piece and partial overlap while re-testing tilts. The incumbent's wedge sentence and its qualitative enters-vs-leaves trade test did not block either. This revision states the containment trap as a general rule (bigger never implies swallowing, and a ratio or a round-looking fraction is not a computed quantity), replaces the trade test with compute-the-simplest-configuration-exactly, and supplies a bound-plus-witness reason that licenses halting.

records.mutation: generalize the cap into a reusable scarce-resource recipe (cap one unit, multiply by unit count) and add a degree audit pinning the per-piece cap at d rather than d-1
records.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts: 3/8 correct. Two failures capped each piece at d-1 roots instead of the stated degree d - an off-by-one in the residual step. Two more abandoned reuse entirely and reported the bare piece count, one after first declaring the count unbounded. One burned all tokens chasing consecutive-difference relations between neighbouring pieces. The three winners all ran the same route: shared affine target, residual roots per piece, multiply by the piece count. So the incumbent's structure is right but two numeric slips survive it. This revision lifts the bound step into a reusable recipe (name the scarce resource, cap one unit, multiply by the unit count) so it transfers past polynomials, adds an explicit degree audit pinning the per-piece cap at d rather than d-1, and states that reuse is permitted unless forbidden to block the retreat to the bare piece count.

records.mutation: add evaluate-from-the-definition rule for logs/exponents (base below one flips the sign) and reframe an apparent inconsistency as that slip rather than a reason to loop
records.subagent_summary: Six of eight fresh rollouts were correct; both failures ran to the token cap on the same mechanical error, not on strategy. Each set up the conditions correctly, solved the reduced quadratic correctly, kept the right root, then evaluated a logarithm with base below one with the wrong sign. The bad value made the recovered vertex fail the substitution check, so the rollout concluded the problem itself was inconsistent and spent thousands of tokens re-expanding the identical algebra, which can never surface an evaluation slip. The incumbent already mandates substitute-back verification but says nothing about what to do when it fails, so I added a transferable rule: evaluate logs/exponents/roots from the definition rather than by pattern-copying, note that a base under one reverses the sign, and treat an apparent contradiction as that slip.

records.mutation: state that which item a step carries is determined by earlier steps (never an independent draw), and route a named-item-at-depth-k event through a short opening block of steps rather than the choose-between-two-readings trace
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent gave 0/8; seven rollouts stopped normally at 7k-15k tokens, so length is not the block. Five of eight reached the free-step count on part one, then every rollout priced the slot part by asserted symmetry, reading off 1/n (or 1/2, or 3!/6 of 4!), and each had first equated the deepest slot with whatever moved last. One collapsed the whole process to certainty and then impossibility. The incumbent asks the student to write both readings of the slot and kill one by tracing a run; it picks a reading and never traces. This revision drops that step and instead states the causal fact the failures violate -- which item a step carries is fixed by the earlier steps, never an independent uniform draw -- gives the upward-growth orientation declaratively, and turns the slot event into a short opening block of steps to price, so the same denominator serves both parts.

records.mutation: add a notation-separation rule (summation label vs condition index) plus a ban on long-product / subset-sum coefficient extraction in favor of evaluating at a convenient point, keeping hand-solved instances as the arbiter over any general form
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling scored 1 of 8; 5 of 8 hit the token cap and the 3 that landed were wrong. The dominant wreck is a notation collapse: rollouts conflated the label being summed over with the index that varies across conditions, so their small hand-solved instance clashed with their own general form. They then either re-derived the same tiny case for thousands of tokens or declared the stated system inconsistent. A second sink is coefficient extraction by brute force: several tried to expand a 2000-plus-factor product or sum products of roots taken all-but-one at a time and never closed. The single success stayed on verified numbers and read the growth rate off them. The incumbent already demands early commitment and small cases but never says how to keep the translation straight or how to lift out one coefficient cheaply, so this revision supplies both.

records.mutation: replace the never-exercised exact-fractions clause with an untried problem-type classification plus canonical-tool recall rule
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts scored reward 1 with clean stops, so train is saturated at 1.0 for the 13th round running and there is no train signal left; every gain must come from transfer, where the incumbent sits at 0.2. The rollouts show the student never exercises the exact-fractions clause (all stage costs are integers and no fraction survives), so that sentence is dead weight and safe to swap. Nineteen rounds of scope-labeling, anti-rumination, output-form, arithmetic-reliability, backward-reasoning and concretization variants all failed to beat it, so I tried the one broadly-applicable move not yet attempted: name the problem class first and recall the canonical tool for that class, since a 1.7B student mostly loses by improvising ad-hoc algebra where a standard technique applies.

records.mutation: compress redundant branch/offset/irrational-center warnings and reinvest in two general guards: a no-symmetry fallback (small concrete cases, extract the invariant) and an ugly-numbers-means-dropped-condition reread rule
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts were correct, each terminating cleanly at 4.1k-8.2k tokens by committing to the shared-center antisymmetric pair, pinning the center by summing the two supplied values, then evaluating inside the centered form. Train is saturated and no failure mode remains to target, so with transfer weighted double the only lever is generality. The revision compresses the redundant branch/offset and irrational-center warnings (the same slip is already covered by the degenerate-center clause) and spends the freed tokens on two guards that fire on problems with no commuting-map structure: when no symmetry exists, work the smallest concrete cases and extract the invariant instead of grinding general algebra; and treat ugly numbers as a signal that a stated condition was dropped, prompting a reread rather than more computation.

records.mutation: add a direct minimality test (confirm the candidate works and that one less fails) so untraced small-period claims are refuted instead of re-audited
records.subagent_summary: Only 3 of 8 rollouts were right. Every failure asserted a repetition count it never ran: three read a count off untraced cycle-type talk (period equals the step count, or one less than the parameter), one guessed a wildly larger power, and two burned the whole budget looping after a bogus 'two passes suffice' claim they kept re-auditing instead of killing. The incumbent already demands a literal run, but says nothing about testing minimality, so the students accepted the first plausible-looking count. The revision keeps the run-outranks-notation core and adds a concrete minimality test: verify the candidate works and that one less does not, which cheaply refutes the small-period guesses that dominate these failures.
